1.1.m: [Guṇa grade and vṛddhi grade do] not [apply] when an ārdhadhātuka affix follows that causes the elision of [part of] a verbal root.
Consonants uninterrupted [by vowels] are called a consonant cluster.
A sound articulated with both mouth and nose is called nasalised.
A dual [inflectional ending ending in] ī, ū, or e is called an uncombinable vowel.
And [words ending in] ī and ū having the meaning of the locative case [are called uncombinable vowels].
Words beginning with svar and particles are called indeclinables.

1.2.m: After [the verbal root] gāṅ and those beginning with kuṭ, an affix having no marker ñ or ṇ is treated as having the marker ṅ.
The affix ktvā following the verbal roots mṛḍ, mṛd, gudh, kuṣ, kliś, vad, and vas [is optionally treated as having the marker k].
And the desiderative affix san following [the verbal roots] rud, vid, muṣ, grah, svap, and pracch [is optionally treated as having the marker k].
A niṣṭhā affix after śīṅ, svid, mid, kṣvid, and dhṛṣ [takes iṭ and is kit].
In the opinion of Kāśyapa, [ktvā is optionally kit] after tṛṣ, mṛṣ, and kṛś.
A vowel whose duration is that of [short, long, or protracted] u (u, ū, u3) is respectively [designated] short vowel, long vowel, [and] protracted vowel.
In calling from afar (dūrāt sambuddhau), [the utterance is] a monotone (ekaśruti).
In sacrificial acts (yajñakarman), except in silent repetition (japa), nyūṅkha recitation, and sāman chants, [the utterance is monotone].
The call vaṣaṭ is optionally (vā) pronounced at a higher pitch.
In deva and brahman, there is low-pitched accent.
In continuous phonological text (saṃhitā), following a circumflex accent, [the substitute is high-pitched accent] for low-pitched accents.
That [low-pitched accent] which is followed by a high-pitched accent or a circumflex accent becomes lower-pitched (sannatara).
That which is designated by the nominative case [in a compounding rule] is [termed] subordinate member (upasarjana) in a compound.
A meaningful [form] that is not a verbal root and not an affix is [termed] nominal stem (prātipadika).
And [forms ending in] primary affixes (kṛt), secondary affixes (taddhita), and compounds are also [termed nominal stem].
In the neuter, a nominal stem takes a short vowel [substitute for its final vowel].
When there is zero-replacement (lup), the gender and number [of the derivative] are like the original thing (yuktavat).
And if the connection were authoritative, upon the absence of that [connection], the non-appearance [of the name] would result.
In expressing a generic class (jāti), the plural is optionally (anyatarasyām) used for the singular.
And [the plural is optionally used for the dual] of phalgunī and proṣṭhapadā denoting asterisms.
In the Veda (chandas), the singular is used for punarvasū.
In a dvandva compound of the asterisms tiṣya and punarvasū, the dual obligatorily replaces the plural.
A senior descendant (vṛddha) [remains alone] with a junior descendant (yuvan), if that distinction is solely based on those [patronymic affixes].
Brother and son [remain alone when paired] with sister and daughter [respectively].
The pronouns beginning with tyad obligatorily [remain alone when paired] with all others.

1.3.m: [After a verbal root with an] anudātta marker or an ṅ marker, [there is] a middle voice ending.
[A middle voice ending is used] in [the sense of] the agent when reciprocity of action [is denoted].
[A middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] krī preceded by pari, vi, or ava.
And [a middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] krīḍ preceded by anu, sam, or pari.
[A middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] sthā preceded by sam, ava, pra, or vi.
[A middle voice ending is used] after gam, ṛcch, pṛcch, svar, ṛ, śru, and vid preceded by sam.
[A middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] nīñ in [the senses of] honouring, tossing up, acting as teacher, knowing, wages, paying off, and spending.
[A middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] kram in [the senses of] uninterrupted continuity, zeal, and expansion.
[A middle voice ending is used after jñā] preceded by sam or prati, when not [in the sense of] recollecting with longing.
[A middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] vad in [the senses of] shining, propitiation, knowledge, exertion, disagreement, and secret solicitation.
[A middle voice ending is used after vad] in [the sense of] simultaneous utterance of articulate speech.
And [a middle voice ending is used] after [the verbal root] dāṇ [preceded by sam, when connected with an instrument in the third case ending] if it is in the sense of the fourth case ending.
[The middle voice ending is used] for the auxiliary verb kṛñ like [the verbal root] followed by the affix ām.

1.3.s: ṇe raṇau yat karma ṇau cet sa kartā 'nādhyāne ||
1.3.d: णे रणौ यत् कर्म णौ चेत् स कर्ता ऽनाध्याने ॥
1.3.m: [The middle voice ending is used] after [a verbal root ending in] ṇi, if that which was the object in the non-causative becomes the agent in the causative, provided there is no longing remembrance.
[The middle voice ending is used after the causatives] of gṛdh and vañc in the sense of deceiving.
[The middle voice ending is used after the causative] of lī also in the senses of honouring and making modest.
[The middle voice ending is used] after kṛñ preceded by the attendant word mithyā, in the sense of repeated action.
[The middle voice ending is used] after [roots marked with] a circumflex accent or with the marker ñ, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent.
[The middle voice ending is used] after yam following sam, ud, or āṅ, when not referring to a book.
From the remainder, the active voice ending [is used] in the sense of the agent.
[The active voice ending is used] after kṣip following abhi, prati, and ati.
[The active voice ending is used after the causative ending in ṇi of a verbal root that is] intransitive in the non-causative and has an animate agent.
Not [the active voice ending after the causatives] of pā, dam, āṅ-yam, āṅ-yas, pari-muh, ruc, nṛt, vad, and vas.

1.4.m: In case of conflict between rules of equal force, the subsequent operational rule prevails.
[The word pati] combined with a genitive is optionally (vā) [termed ghi] in the Veda.
That which begins with [the element] after which an affix is ordained is [termed] the stem base (aṅga) when that affix follows.
The one whom [the agent] aims to reach by means of the object is [called] sampradāna (recipient).
In the case of [the roots] ślāgh ('to praise'), hnuṅ ('to conceal'), sthā ('to stay/reveal oneself'), and śap ('to curse/swear'), the one whom it is desired to inform [is called sampradāna].
In the case of [the roots] rādh and īkṣ ('to inquire about future fortune'), the one concerning whom questions are asked [is called sampradāna].
In the case of [the root] śru preceded by prati or āṅ, the agent of the previous [action of entreaty is called sampradāna].
kaṇe and manas [are called gati] in the sense of satisfying a desire.
accha [is called gati] in connection with [roots] meaning motion, and with the root vad ('to speak').
urasi and manasi [are called gati in connection with kṛñ] when placing into is not literal.
madhye, pade, and nivacane [are called gati in connection with kṛñ].
[The particles] prati, pari, and anu [are called karmapravacanīya] in [the meanings of] sign (lakṣaṇa), stating a state of being such (itthaṃbhūtākhyāna), portion (bhāga), and distribution (vīpsā).
Prati [is also called karmapravacanīya] in [the meanings of] representative and exchange.
The tiṅ [endings taken] three by three are the third (prathama), second (madhyama), and first (uttama) persons.
These [triads], one by one, are singular (ekavacana), dual (dvivacana), and plural (bahuvacana).

1.4.s: prahāse ca manya-upapade manyater uttama ekavac ca ||
1.4.d: प्रहासे च मन्य-उपपदे मन्यतेर् उत्तम एकवच् च ॥

1.4.m: The closest proximity [between sounds] is continuous phonological text (saṃhitā).

2.1.m: An indeclinable (avyaya) [compounds with an inflected word] in the meanings of case-ending, proximity, prosperity, adversity, non-existence of an object, passing away, not at the present time, appearance of sound, after, according to, order, simultaneity, likeness, attainment, entirety, and end.
Apa, pari, bahis, and words ending in añc [compound] with [a word ending in] the ablative (pañcamī).
And [irregularly formed words such as] tiṣṭhadgu and the like [are avyayībhāva compounds].
[A word ending in the instrumental compounds] with [the words] pūrva, sadṛśa, sama, those having the meaning of ūna ('less'), kalaha, nipuṇa, miśra, and ślakṣṇa.
[A word denoting] an ingredient [in the instrumental compounds] with [a word denoting] food [eaten] after mixing.
pūrvakāla ('prior in time'), eka ('one'), sarva ('all'), jarat ('old'), purāṇa ('ancient'), nava ('new'), and kevala ('alone') [compound] with a coreferential [word].
[Words expressing] standards of comparison [compound] with words expressing a common property.

And pūrva ('prior'), apara ('subsequent'), prathama ('first'), carama ('last'), jaghanya ('lowest'), samāna ('equal'), madhya ('middle'), madhyama ('intermediate'), and vīra ('brave') [compound with the modified].
[A word denoting a thing that is] praised [compounds] with vṛndāraka ('distinguished'), nāga ('elephant'), and kuñjara ('elephant').
katara ('which of the two') and katama ('which of many') [compound with a coreferential word] in an inquiry regarding class.

[A word denoting] a class [compounds] with poṭā ('hermaphrodite'), yuvati ('young woman'), stoka ('small'), katipaya ('a few'), gṛṣṭi ('cow calving once'), dhenu ('milch-cow'), vaśā ('barren cow'), vehad ('miscarrying cow'), baṣkayaṇī ('cow with calf grown'), pravaktṛ ('teacher'), śrotriya ('learned brāhmaṇa'), adhyāpaka ('instructor'), and dhūrta ('crafty').

2.2.m: And prāpta ('reached') and āpanna ('arrived at') [compound] with [a word ending in] the accusative [case].

[A word ending in the genitive case does not compound] with [words ending in] an ordinal affix, [words expressing] quality, words meaning 'satiated', the affix sat (śatṛ and śānac), indeclinables, the affix tavya, and a coreferential [word].
[A word ending in the genitive case] obligatorily [compounds with a word ending in aka] in [reference to] sport or livelihood.

2.3.m: The seventh and fifth inflectional endings [are used] to denote [the interval of time or distance] between two participants in an action (kāraka).
The second inflectional ending [is used] in connection with a prepositional particle (karmapravacanīya).

2.3.s: yasmād adhikaṃ yasya ca+īśvara-vacanaṃ tatra saptamī ||
2.3.d: यस्माद् अधिकं यस्य च+ईश्वर-वचनं तत्र सप्तमी ॥

2.3.m: And [the fifth inflectional ending is used] from that which is a substitute or a return-exchange.
The second and fourth inflectional endings [are used] for the object of verbs of going, when bodily motion is meant and [the object is] not a road.
And [the fourth inflectional ending is used] after [a word] expressing an action having the sense of the affix 'tum' (infinitive).
And [the fourth inflectional ending is used] in connection with 'namaḥ', 'svasti', 'svāhā', 'svadhā', 'alam', and 'vaṣaṭ'.
[The fourth inflectional ending is applied] optionally (vibhāṣā) to the object of [the verb] 'man' (to think) when contempt is expressed, [provided the object] is an inanimate entity.
The third inflectional ending [is used] in [denoting] the agent (kartṛ) and the instrument (karaṇa).
The sixth inflectional ending [is used in connection] with an affix having the sense of 'atas'.
The third inflectional ending [is used] optionally (anyatarasyām) [along with the second and fifth] in connection with 'pṛthak', 'vinā', and 'nānā'.
And [the seventh inflectional ending is used after a word] whose action indicates another action.
And [the sixth or seventh inflectional ending is used] in connection with 'svāmin', 'īśvara', 'adhipati', 'dāyāda', 'sākṣin', 'pratibhū', and 'prasūta'.
The seventh inflectional ending [is used] in connection with 'sādhu' and 'nipuṇa' when respect is meant, except with 'prati'.
The first inflectional ending [is used] merely to express the nominal stem meaning, gender, measure, and number.
[The sixth inflectional ending is used] in the instrument of [the verbal root] jñā when it does not mean 'to know'.
[The sixth inflectional ending is used in the object] of jāsi, pra-han with ni, nāṭ, krāth, and piṣ in [the sense of] injuring.
[The sixth inflectional ending is used in the object] of vy-ava-hṛ and paṇ when they have the same meaning.
[The sixth inflectional ending is used] for the sacrificial offering in connection with preṣya and brū when a deity is the indirect object.
[The sixth inflectional ending is used] diversely in sacred texts in the sense of the fourth inflectional ending.
[The sixth inflectional ending is used] in the location of time when a word having the sense of kṛtvas is employed.
When both apply, [the sixth inflectional ending is used] in the object.

2.4.m: [A dvandva compound of] Adhvaryu sacrifices that is not neuter [is singular in number].
Rivers and regions of distinct genders that are not villages [form a dvandva compound that is singular in number].
And [a dvandva compound of entities] whose hostility is eternal [is singular in number].
[A dvandva compound] of Śūdras who have not been expelled [is singular in number].
[Singular number is] an optional rule (vibhāṣā) for [dvandva compounds of] trees, wild beasts, grasses, grains, condiments, cattle, birds, aśvavaḍava, and pūrvāpara and adharottara.
A tatpuruṣa compound, except a negative or a karmadhāraya compound, [ending in kanta is neuter].
[Being neuter is] an optional rule (vibhāṣā) for [tatpuruṣa compounds ending in] senā, surā, chāyā, śālā, and niśā.
The gender of dvandva and tatpuruṣa compounds is like that of the subsequent member.
jagdhi is [the substitute] of ad before lyap and a kit affix beginning with t.
Optionally (anyatarasyām) before middle voice endings [in luṅ].
There are substitutes Agasti and Kuṇḍinac for Āgastya and Kauṇḍinya [respectively, in the plural].
[There is zero-replacement (luk)] of nominal case endings (sup) inside a verbal root or a nominal stem.
[There is zero-replacement (luk)] of [the infix] śap after Ad and the rest.
[There is zero-replacement (luk)] of [the aorist marker] sic after [roots ending in] gā, sthā, ghu [roots], pā, and bhū, before active voice endings.

2.4.d: न अव्ययीभावाद् अतो ऽम् त्व् अपञ्चम्याः ॥

2.4.m: Variously for the instrumental and locative case endings [after an avyayībhāva compound ending in a].
There are substitutes ḍā, rau, and ras for the third person endings of luṭ [in active voice].

3.1.m: Optionally (vā) [the affix san occurs] after a verbal root that is the object of wishing and shares the same agent, in the sense of desire.
[The affix kyaṅ occurs] after words of the bhṛśa class in the sense of 'becoming' when cvi is not used, and there is elision of a final consonant.
[The affix] kyaṣ occurs after words of the lohita class and words ending in ḍāc [in the sense of 'becoming'].
[The affix kyaṅ occurs] after romantha and tapas denoting the direct object when construed with the roots vart ('chew') and car ('perform') respectively.
[The affix kyaṅ occurs] after sukha and similar words when signifying the experience of the agent.
[The affix] kyac occurs after namas, varivas, and citraṅa [in the sense of performing].
[The affix] ṇic occurs after muṇḍa, miśra, ślakṣṇa, lavaṇa, vrata, vastra, hala, kala, kṛta, and tūsta [in specified verbal senses].
[The affix yaṅ occurs] after lup, sad, car, jap, jabh, dah, daś, and gṝ to express censure of the action.
[The affix] ṇic occurs after satya, āpa, pāśa, rūpa, vīṇā, tūla, śloka, senā, loman, tvac, varman, varṇa, cūrṇa, and the roots of the cur class.
[The affix] āya occurs after gup, dhūp, vicch, paṇ, and pan.
The affixes beginning with āya [are added] optionally (vā) before an ārdhadhātuka affix.
[The affix] ām occurs before liṭ, in non-Vedic usage, after the root kās and after roots ending in an affix.
And [ām occurs] after a root beginning with an ic vowel and having a heavy syllable, except ṛcch.
[The affix ām occurs] optionally (anyatarasyām) after uṣ, vid, and jāgṛ.
And [roots] bhī, hrī, bhṛ, and hu behave as if taking ślu [when ām follows].
The form vidāṅkurvantu occurs optionally (anyatarasyām) [in the imperative].
In the Veda, the forms abhyutsādayām akaḥ, prajanayām akaḥ, cikayām akaḥ, ramayām akaḥ, pāvayām kriyāt, and vidām akran occur.
Kṣa is the substitute [for cli] after [a root] ending in a śal consonant, having an ik vowel as penultimate, and not taking the augment iṭ.
[Caṅ is] not [substituted for cli] after unayati, dhvanayati, elayati, and ardayati.
Aṅ is the substitute [for cli] after as, vac, and khyā.
Optionally (anyatarasyām) before middle voice endings.
And [aṅ is substituted for cli] after sṛ, śās, and ṛ.
And [aṅ is substituted for cli] after jṝ, stambh, mruc, mluc, gruc, gluc, gluñc, and śvi.
In the Veda, [aṅ is substituted for cli] after kṛ, mṛ, dṛ, and ruh.
[Ciṇ is substituted before ta] optionally (anyatarasyām) after dīp, jan, budh, pūr, tāy, and pyāy.
[The affix śyan occurs] optionally (vā) after bhrāś, bhlāś, bhram, kram, klam, tras, truṭ, and laṣ.
And after the roots stambhu, stumbhu, skambhu, skumbhu, and skuñ, the affix śnu [is introduced as well as śnā].
[An agent] whose action is identical with that of an object is treated like an object.
The affixes yak and ciṇ are not [introduced] after duh, snu, and nam [when treated like an object].
According to the Eastern teachers, after the roots kuṣ and raj, the affix śyan and the active voice ending (parasmaipada) [are used].
The forms avadya, paṇya, and varya are irregularly formed in the senses of blameworthy, to be bartered, and non-confinement respectively.
The forms upasaryā and kālyā are irregularly formed in the sense of being fit for breeding.
After the roots i, stu, śās, vṛ, dṛ, and juṣ, the affix kyap [is introduced].
The words rājasūya, sūrya, mṛṣodya, rucya, kupya, kṛṣṭapacya, and avyathya are irregularly formed.
The forms puṣya and siddhya are irregularly formed denoting an asterism (nakṣatra).
The forms vipūya, vinīya, and jityā are irregularly formed denoting muñja grass, sediment, and a ploughshare respectively.
In the Veda, after the root grah preceded by prati and api, [the affix kyap is introduced].
The form amāvasyā is irregularly formed optionally (anyatarasyām).

In the Veda, the forms niṣṭarkya, devahūya, praṇīya, unnīya, ucchiṣya, marya, starya, dhvarya, khanya, khānya, devayajyā, āpṛcchya, pratiṣīvya, brahmavādya, bhāvya, stāvya, and upacāyyapṛḍa are irregularly formed.
And [the affix ṇyat is introduced] after ā-su, yu, vap, rap, lap, trap, and cam.
The forms pāyya, sānnāyya, nikāyya, and dhāyyā are irregularly formed in the senses of a measure, sacrificial oblation, a dwelling, and a sāmidhenī verse respectively.
[The affixes] lyu, ṇini, and ac [occur respectively] after [the verbal roots of] the classes beginning with nandi, grah, and pac.
[The affix] ka occurs after [a verbal root] with an ik vowel as penultimate, and after [the verbal roots] jñā, prī, and kṝ.
And without a preverb, after limp, vind, dhāri, pāri, vedi, udeji, ceti, sāti, and sāhi.
Optionally (vibhāṣā) after [the verbal roots] dadāti and dadhāti.
[The affix] ṇa occurs after [verbal roots] from jval onward and those ending in the affix kas.
[The affix] vun occurs after pru, sṛ, and lū in the sense of repetition/intensity (samabhihāra).

3.2.m: After ram and jap when stamba and karṇa [are the respective attendant words].
After sṛ when puras, agratas, or agre is the attendant word.

[The affix ṭa occurs after kṛñ] when divā, vibhā, niśā, prabhā, bhās, kāra, anta, ananta, ādi, bahu, nāndī, kim, lipi, libi, bali, bhakti, kartṛ, citra, kṣetra, saṅkhyā, jaṅghā, bāhu, ahar, yad, tad, dhanus, or arus [is the attendant word].
Not when the words śabda, śloka, kalaha, gāthā, vaira, cāṭu, sūtra, mantra, or pada [are the attendant words].
After hṛ when dṛti or nātha is the attendant word, denoting an animal.
And phalegrahi and ātmambhari [are irregularly derived].
In the sacred texts (chandas), after van, san, rakṣ, and math.
After dhmā and dheṭ when nāsikā and stana [are the respective attendant words].
After dṛś and tap when asūrya and lalāṭa [are the respective attendant words].
After dāri and sah when pūr and sarva [are the respective attendant words].
[The affix khas is introduced] after [the verbal root] kṛñ ('to do, make'), when megha, ṛti, or bhaya [co-occur as the object attendant word].
[The affix khas is introduced] after [the verbal root] bhū ('to be, become'), when āśita ('satiated') [co-occurs as attendant word], to denote the instrument or the action.
[The affix khas is introduced] after [the verbal roots] bhṛ, tṝ, vṛ, ji, the causal of dhṛ (dhāri), sah, tap, and dam, when [the derivative denotes] a technical term / name.
[The affix ṭak is introduced after han] in the sense of capacity, when hastin or kapāṭa [co-occurs as the object attendant word].
The forms pāṇigha and tāḍagha are irregularly derived [with ṭak after han] to designate an artisan.

3.2.d: आढ्य-सुभग-स्थूल-पलित-नग्न-अन्ध-प्रियेषु च्व्य्-अर्थेष्व् अच्वौ कृञः करणे ख्युन् ॥

3.2.m: The affixes khiṣṇuc and khukañ are introduced in the sense of an agent after [the verbal root] bhū [under the same attendant conditions].
And [the affix kvin is introduced after the verbal roots in] ṛtvij, dadhṛṣ, sraj, diś, uṣṇih, añc, yuj, and kruñc [irregularly].
And after [the verbal root] dṛś ('to see'), when tyad and the rest [co-occur as attendant words] and [mental] perception is not meant, [the affix kvin is introduced], and also kañ.
The affix kvip is introduced after sad, sū, dviṣ, druh, duh, yuj, vid, bhid, chid, ji, nī, and rāj, even when preceded by a preverb.
[The affix] ñyuṭ is introduced [after vah] when kavya, purīṣa, or purīṣya [co-occur as the object attendant word].
[The affix] viṭ is introduced after jan, san, khan, kram, and gam.
And after [roots ending in] long ā, the affixes manin, kvanip, and vanip are introduced.
[The affix] ṇini is introduced after [a verbal root] when an inflected nominal word (sup) that is not a generic term co-occurs as attendant word, to denote habitual nature.
[The affix] kvip is introduced [after han in the past] when brahma, bhrūṇa, or vṛtra [co-occur as the object attendant word].
[The affix ṇini is introduced] after [the verbal root] kṛñ, when su, karman, pāpa, mantra, or puṇya [co-occur as the object attendant word, in the past].
In classical speech, [kvasu optionally replaces liṭ] after the verbal roots sad- ('to sit'), vas- ('to dwell'), and śru- ('to hear').
And the forms upeyivān, anāśvān, and anūcāna are irregularly formed [in the past tense].
[Laṭ occurs with sma] in answering a question with nanu.
The affixes śatṛ and śānac replace laṭ when standing in grammatical agreement with a word not in the nominative case.
[Śatṛ and śānac replace laṭ] to signify a characteristic sign (lakṣaṇa) or cause (hetu) of another action.
The affix śatṛ occurs after iṅ- ('to study') and dhāri- ('to owe') when denoting a person in difficulty (kṛcchrin).

Up to [sūtra 3.2.178, 'kveḥ'], the following affixes are taught in the senses of having that as one's natural disposition (tacchīla), having that as one's duty (taddharma), or performing that action well (tatsādhukārin).
The affix iṣṇuc occurs after alaṅ-kṛñ-, nirā-kṛñ-, pra-jan-, ut-pac-, ut-pat-, un-mad-, ruc-, apa-trap-, vṛt-, vṛdh-, sah-, and car-.
The affix knu occurs after tras- ('to tremble'), gṛdh- ('to be greedy'), dhṛṣ- ('to dare'), and kṣip- ('to throw').
The affix ghinuṇ occurs after the eight roots beginning with śam- ('to be calm').
[Ghinuṇ occurs] when preceded by vi-, after kaṣ-, las-, katth-, and srambh-.
[Ghinuṇ occurs] after lap-, sṛ-, dru-, math-, vad-, and vas-, when preceded by pra-.
The affix vuñ occurs after nind-, hiṃs-, kliś-, khād-, vināśi-, parikṣip-, pariraṭ-, parivādi-, vyābhāṣ-, and asūy-.
The affix yuc occurs after an intransitive root meaning motion or sound.
[Yuc occurs] after ju-, caṅkramya-, dandramya-, sṛ-, gṛdh-, jval-, śuc-, laṣ-, pat-, and pad-.
The affix ukañ occurs after laṣ-, pat-, pad-, sthā-, bhū-, vṛṣ-, han-, kam-, gam-, and śṝ-.
The affix ṣākan occurs after jalp-, bhikṣ-, kuṭṭ-, luṇṭ-, and vṛñ-.
The affix ghurac occurs after bhañj-, bhās-, and mid-.
The affix kurac is introduced after the verbal roots vid- 'to know', bhid- 'to split', and chid- 'to cut'.
The affix kvarap is introduced after the verbal roots iṇ- 'to go', naś- 'to perish', ji- 'to conquer', and sṛ- 'to run'.
The affix raḥ is introduced after the verbal roots nam- 'to bow', kamp- 'to tremble', smi- 'to smile', ajas- 'not to cease', kam- 'to desire', hiṃs- 'to harm', and dīp- 'to shine'.
The affixes ki and kin are introduced after verbal roots ending in ā, and after ṛ- 'to go', gam- 'to go', han- 'to strike', and jan- 'to be born', and the augment liṭ [reduplication] takes place.

The affix ṣṭran is introduced after the verbal roots dā- 'to cut', nī- 'to lead', śas- 'to cut', yu- 'to bind', yuj- 'to join', stu- 'to praise', tud- 'to strike', si- 'to bind', sic- 'to sprinkle', mih- 'to urinate', pat- 'to fall', daś- 'to bite', and nah- 'to tie', to designate an instrument.
The affix itraḥ is introduced after the verbal roots ṛ- 'to go', lū- 'to cut', dhū- 'to shake', sū- 'to yield', khan- 'to dig', sah- 'to endure', and car- 'to move', to designate an instrument.
The affix itraḥ is also introduced after the verbal root pū- to designate the agent when naming a seer or a deity.

3.3.m: The forms gamya- and others are irregularly formed in the future tense.
The tense affix laṭ is introduced in the future tense when connected with the particles yāvat or purā.
The affix ghañ is introduced after the verbal roots pad- 'to fall', ruj- 'to break', viś- 'to enter', and spṛś- 'to touch'.
[The affix ghañ occurs] after śī- 'to lie down' when preceded by vi- and upa-, [in the sense of] succession.
In [the sense of] reciprocity of action, [the affix] ṇac [occurs after a verbal root] in the feminine.
[The affix ghañ occurs] after śri- 'to resort to', yu- 'to unite', pū- 'to purify', and dru- 'to run', when preceded by ut-.
[The affix ghañ occurs] after grah- 'to seize' when preceded by ava-, in [the sense of] cessation of rain.
And [the affix ap occurs] after grah- 'to seize', vr̥- 'to choose', dr̥- 'to tear', ni-ści- 'to decide', and gam- 'to go'.
[The affix ap occurs] after vyadh- 'to pierce' and jap- 'to whisper' when not preceded by a prefix (upasarga).
[The affix ap occurs] after gad- 'to speak', nad- 'to roar', paṭh- 'to recite', and svan- 'to sound', when preceded by ni-.
[The forms] pramada and sammada [are irregularly formed with ap] in [the sense of] joy.
And vocalisation (samprasāraṇa) [is substituted] for hve- 'to call' [with ap] when preceded by ni-, abhi-, upa-, and vi-.
[The affix] naṅ occurs after yaj- 'to sacrifice', yāc- 'to ask', yat- 'to strive', vicch- 'to shine/go', pracch- 'to ask', and rakṣ- 'to protect'.
And [the words] ūti, yūti, jūti, sāti, heti, and kīrti [are formed with ktin bearing a high-pitched accent].
[The affix kyap occurs] when a technical name (sañjñā) [is denoted], after sam-aj-, ni-ṣad-, ni-pat-, man-, vid-, ṣuñ-, śīṅ-, bhṛñ-, and iṇ-.
And [the affix aṅ occurs in the feminine] after cint-, pūj-, kath-, kumb-, and carc-.

3.3.s: karmaṇi ca yena saṃsparśāt kartuḥ śarīra-sukham ||
3.3.d: कर्मणि च येन संस्पर्शात् कर्तुः शरीर-सुखम् ॥
3.3.m: And [the affixes kta and lyuṭ occur] in the sense of the object (karman) [denoting that] from contact with which bodily pleasure arises for the agent.
And [the affix khal occurs after īṣat, dur, and su] in the sense of the agent or the object after bhū- and kṛñ-.
In the Veda (chandas), [the affix khal occurs] after roots signifying motion.
When proximity to the present is meant, [a tense/mood affix may be used] optionally (vā) as if [denoting] the present.
When continuity of action or proximity [is meant], [an affix] does not behave as denoting non-current day (anadyatana).
In the future, when expressing a boundary (maryādā), [it behaves as anadyatanavat] with respect to the nearer [division of time].
When censure (garhā) is meant, [the affix] laṭ (present) [occurs] in connection with api and jātu.
When making known a desire (kāmapravedana), [the affix liṅ occurs], provided that kaccit is not [connected].
[The affix liṅ occurs] optionally (vibhāṣā) when a verbal root expressing possibility [is used], unless yadi ('if') [is present].
[The affix] tumun [occurs] when [the actions have] the same agent.
[The affixes occur] optionally (vibhāṣā) after [roots] meaning 'wish' in the present [tense].
[The affix] tumun [occurs] when [the upapadas] kāla, samaya, and velā ('time') [are present].

3.4.m: Affixes [denote time] in connection with [another] verbal root.

3.4.s: kriyāsam-abhihāre loṭ loṭo hi-svau vā ca ta-dhvamoḥ ||
3.4.d: क्रियासम्-अभिहारे लोट् लोटो हि-स्वौ वा च त-ध्वमोः ॥

3.4.m: According to the rule, a subsequent application [of a root occurs] after the former.
In combination, [the subsequent application is] of a [root] expressing general action.
In the sense of tumun, [the affixes] se, sen, ase, asen, kṣe, kasen, adhyai, adhyain, kadhyai, kadhyain, śadhyai, śadhyain, tavai, taveṅ, and taven [occur in the Veda].
[The forms] prayai, rohiṣyai, and avyathiṣyai [are valid in the Veda in the sense of tumun].
When indicating a state (bhāva-lakṣaṇa), [the affix] tosun [occurs] after [the roots] sthā, iṇ, kṛñ, vad, car, hu, tam, and jan.
[The affix] ktvā [occurs] in prohibition with alam and khalu, according to the eastern grammarians (prāñc).
Optionally (vibhāṣā) when agre, prathama, and pūrva [are the upapadas].
[The affix] khamuñ [occurs] after kṛñ in reviling, when the object is [the upapada].
When yathā and tathā [are the upapadas], in a reply showing malice.
After dṛś and vid, when the object [is the upapada], in the sense of entirety.
After kaṣ, when nimūla and samūla [are the upapada objects].
After piṣ, when śuṣka, cūrṇa, and rūkṣa [are the upapada objects].
In the case of [roots] beginning with kaṣ- ('to scrape'), there is an ensuing application [of the finite verb] in accordance with the rule.
[The affix ṇamul occurs] after [the verbal roots] as- ('to cast') and tṛṣ- ('to thirst'), when [the attendant word expresses] time denoting another action.
[The affixes ktvā and ṇamul occur] after [the verbal roots] kṛ- ('to do') and bhū- ('to become'), when [the attendant word denotes] one's own limb ending in the affix -tas.

The affix tumun occurs in the sense of [the verbal roots] śak- ('to be able'), dhṛṣ- ('to dare'), jñā- ('to know'), glā- ('to be weary'), ghaṭ- ('to strive'), rabh- ('to begin'), labh- ('to obtain'), kram- ('to proceed'), sah- ('to endure'), arh- ('to deserve'), and as- ('to be').
[The affix tumun occurs] in words expressing sufficiency that have the sense of alam.

3.4.s: laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve ca akramakebhyaḥ ||
3.4.d: लः कर्मणि च भावे च अक्रमकेभ्यः ॥

3.4.m: The kṛtya affixes, the affix kta, and affixes having the sense of khal occur only in those two [senses, namely the object and the verbal action].
The affix kta occurs in the sense of the beginning of an action, and also in [the sense of] the agent.
And the affix kta occurs in [the sense of] the locus after [roots] having the sense of immobility, motion, or eating.
In the case of [an l-affix] with the marker ṭ, [the substitute] e replaces the final vowel along with any following consonant (ṭi) of the middle voice endings.
āha is the substitute of [the verbal root] brū- ('to speak') before the first five [replacements of liṭ replacing laṭ].
And there is elision of i in active voice endings [of leṭ].
And [jus is the substitute of jhi] after sic, a reduplicated base, and the root vid-.

4.1.m: Su, au, jas, am, auṭ, śas, ṭā, bhyām, bhis, ṅe, bhyām, bhyas, ṅasi, bhyām, bhyas, ṅas, os, ām, ṅi, os, sup [occur as inflectional endings].
Ḍāp [occurs] optionally after both [man and a bahuvrīhi ending in an].
Everywhere [ṣpha occurs] after the lohita group and [words ending in] kata.
And [ṣpha occurs] after kauravya and māṇḍūka.
[Ṅīp does] not [occur] after [a dvigu compound denoting] a measure, or bista, ācita, and kambalya, when there is zero-replacement (luk) of a secondary affix.
[Ṅīp occurs] optionally after [a dvigu compound ending in] puruṣa when denoting a measure.
[Ṅīp occurs] optionally after [a bahuvrīhi ending in] an that undergoes elision of the penultimate [vowel].
Nuk [is the augment] of antarvat and pativat.
N is the substitute of [the ending sound of] pati when expressing a sacrificial connection.
[Ai is the augment] of vṛṣākapi, agni, kusita, and kusida, and is high-pitched.

[The affix ṅīṣ occurs] after jānapada, kuṇḍa, goṇa, sthala, bhāja, nāga, kāla, nīla, kuśa, kāmuka, and kabara, when expressing respectively an occupation, a vessel, a receptacle for sowing, not artificial, cooked food, thickness, color, not a garment, an iron utensil, desire for sexual intercourse, and an arrangement of hair.
The augment ānuk occurs before [ṅīṣ] after indra, varuṇa, bhava, śarva, rudra, mṛḍa, hima, araṇya, yava, yavana, mātula, and ācārya.
And [the affix ṅīṣ does not occur after a bahuvrīhi compound denoting a body part] preceded by saha, nañ, or vidyamāna.
And the form dīrghajihvī [is valid] in the Veda.
And [the affix ṅīṣ occurs after a stem denoting a genus] whose final member is pāka, karṇa, parṇa, puṣpa, phala, mūla, or vāla.
[The affix ūṅ occurs] after kadru and kamaṇḍalu in the Veda.
[The affix ṣyaṅ occurs] optionally (anyatarasyām) after daivayajñi, śaucivṛkṣi, sātyamugri, and kāṇṭheviddhi.
[A secondary affix occurs] optionally (vā) after the first of syntactically related words.
[The affix] ṇya occurs after diti, aditi, āditya, and [compounds] whose final member is pati.
[The affixes] nañ and snañ [occur] respectively after strī and puṃs, up to [aphorism 4.2.37] 'bhavana'.
There is [zero-replacement (luk)] optionally (anyatarasyām) after [the affixes] phak and phiñ.
[The affix phak occurs] after śaradvat, śunaka, and darbha, when [the descendant belongs to the gotras of] the Bhṛgus, the Vatsas, and the Āgrāyaṇas [respectively].
[The affix phak occurs] optionally (anyatarasyām) after droṇa, parvata, and jīvanta.
[The affix aṇ occurs] after stems that are not vṛddha, denoting rivers or mortal women, provided they bear their [proper] names.
And [the affix aṇ occurs] after stems denoting seers, Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis, and Kurus.
[The affix ḍhak occurs] after vikarṇa and kuṣītaka, when denoting a Kāśyapa.
And [the affix] ṇa [occurs] after [a feminine stem expressing] a gotra-woman, in the sense of censure.
[The affix] ṭhak [occurs] variously (bahulam) after a vṛddha stem, among the Sauvīras.
And [the affix ṇya occurs] after [names of warrior clans] ending in senā and after markers.
And [the affix phiñ occurs] after kauśalya and kārmārya.
In the view of the Northerners, [the affix phiñ occurs] after a vṛddha stem that does not designate a gotra.
[The affix phiñ occurs] optionally (anyatarasyām) after [a stem] ending in putra.
In the view of the Easterners, [the affix] phin [occurs] variously (bahulam) after a stem that is not vṛddha.
After a word denoting a country (janapada) that is also [the name of] a Kṣatriya [tribe], the affix añ occurs [in the sense of offspring/ruler].
And after sālveya and gāndhārī [the affix añ occurs].
After a dissyllabic stem, and after magadha, kaliṅga, and sūramasa, the affix aṇ occurs.
After names of parts of Sālva, and after pratyagratha, kalakūṭa, and aśmaka, the affix iñ occurs.
And in the feminine, after avanti, kunti, and kuru [there is zero-replacement (luk) of a tadrāja affix].

4.2.m: After lākṣā, rocanā, śakala, and kardama, the affix ṭhak occurs.
After sthaṇḍila, [the affix occurs] when denoting an ascetic vow of lying [on bare ground].
After āgrahāyaṇī and aśvatthī, the affix ṭhak occurs.
Optionally (vibhāṣā) after phālgunī, śravaṇā, kārtikī, and caitrī [the affix ṭhak occurs].
And after dyāvāpṛthivī, śunāsīra, marutvat, agnīṣoma, vāstoṣpati, and gṛhamedha, the affix cha occurs.
After mahārāja and proṣṭhapada, the affix ṭhañ occurs.
The words pitṛvya, mātula, mātāmaha, and pitāmaha are irregularly formed.
After brāhmaṇa, māṇava, and vāḍava, the affix yañ occurs.
[The affix] tal [occurs] after [the stems] grāma, jana, bandhu, and sahāya [in the sense of a collection].
[The affix] ṭhak [occurs] after an inanimate object (acitta), hastin, and dhenu [in the sense of a collection].
[The affixes] vidhal and bhaktal [occur] respectively after [stems] beginning with bhauriki and aiṣukāri [in the sense of "its domain"].

4.2.s: tad asyāṃ praharaṇam iti krīḍāyāṃ ṇaḥ ||
4.2.d: तद् अस्यां प्रहरणम् इति क्रीडायां णः ॥
4.2.m: [The affix] ṇa occurs in the sense of: "That is the weapon (praharaṇa) therein," with reference to a game (krīḍā).
[The affix] ña occurs after [a stem ending in the affix] ghañ in the sense of: "That action (kriyā) is [performed] therein" [with reference to a game].

4.2.s: tad asminn asti iti deśe tannāmni ||
4.2.d: तद् अस्मिन्न् अस्ति इति देशे तन्नाम्नि ॥

4.2.m: [The affix añ occurs after stems] in the feminine gender among the Sauvīras, the Sālvas, and in the eastern country.
[The affix] ḍmatup occurs after kumuda, naḍa, and vetasa.
[The affix] tyak occurs after dakṣiṇā, paścāt, and puras.
[The affix] yat occurs after dyu, prāñc, apāñc, udañc, and pratyañc.
And [añ occurs] after [a stem denoting] a northern village, having many syllables and having an acute accent on the final vowel.
[The affix aṇ does] not [occur] after a disyllabic stem when denoting easterners or Bharatas.
[The affixes] ṭhañ and ñiṭha occur after Kāśi and others.
And [vuñ occurs] after [a stem] ending in prastha, pura, or vaha [denoting a country].
And [vuñ occurs after stems denoting] a country or its boundary.
[vuñ occurs] even after a stem not termed vṛddha, when its domain of application is the plural.
[vuñ occurs] after nagara when expressing censure or proficiency.
An optional rule (vibhāṣā) applies [for vuñ] after Kuru and Yugandhara.

4.3.m: And [the affix] khañ optionally (anyatarasyām) occurs after yuṣmad and asmad.
tavaka and mamaka [are the substitutes] in the singular.
[The affix] yañ occurs after dvīpa when along the sea.
After the indeclinables sāya-, cira-, prāhṇe, [and] prage, [the affixes] ṭyu and ṭyul [are introduced], and [there is] the augment tut.
After sindhu and apakara, [the affix] kan [is introduced].
Zero-replacement (luk) [of the affix occurs] after śraviṣṭhā, phālgunī, anurādhā, svāti, tiṣya, punarvasu, hasta, viśākhā, aṣāḍhā, and bahulā.
[The affix also occurs with the senses:] 'made', 'obtained', 'bought', or 'skilled' [therein].
[The affix occurs] after a time-denoting stem with the senses: 'suitable', 'blossoming', or 'ripening' [therein].
After kalāpī, aśvattha, and yavabusa, [the affix] vun [is introduced].
After dṛti, kukṣi, kalaśi, vasti, asti, and ahi, [the affix] ḍhañ [is introduced].
When not designating a sound, [the affixes] yat and kha occur optionally (anyatarasyām).
And [the affix occurs] after the name of the subject to be explained with the sense: 'its commentary' (tasya vyākhyānaḥ).
After a disyllabic stem, one ending in ṛ, brāhmaṇa, ṛc, prathama, adhvara, and puraścaraṇa-nāmākhyāta, [the affix] ṭhak [is introduced].
[The affix] rūpya occurs optionally (anyatarasyām) after [stems denoting] causes and humans.
[The affix occurs with the sense:] 'goes thither', with reference to a road or a messenger.
[The affix occurs with the sense:] 'opens towards it', with reference to a gate.
[The affix occurs with the sense:] 'in a composition composed concerning that'.
[The affix] cha occurs after [names of] warrior tribes residing in the mountains.
[The affix] ṭhak occurs after an inanimate stem that does not denote place or time.

4.3.s: janapadināṃ janapadavat sarvaṃ janapadena samānaśabdānāṃ bahuvacane ||
4.3.d: जनपदिनां जनपदवत् सर्वं जनपदेन समानशब्दानां बहुवचने ॥
4.3.m: The forms denoting inhabitants of a country are in all respects like the country itself, when in the plural they share the identical word with the country.
[The affix] ṇini occurs after the two seers kāśyapa and kauśika.
[The affix ṇini occurs] with reference to Brāhmaṇas and Kalpas proclaimed by ancient seers.
[The affix occurs] after pārāśarya and śilālin with reference to the aphorisms for mendicants (bhikṣusūtra) and actors (naṭasūtra) [respectively].
[The affix] ini occurs after karmanda and kṛśāśva [with reference to the aphorisms for mendicants and actors respectively].
[The affix] añ [occurs] after kṣudrā, bhramara, vaṭara, and pādapa.
And [in the sense of] 'a part of it' after words denoting living beings, herbs, and trees.
[The affix aṇ occurs] after gold stems (jātarūpa) when denoting a measure.
[The affixes] yañ and añ [occur respectively] to form kaṃsīya and paraśavya, and there is zero-replacement (luk).

4.4.m: [The affix ṭhak occurs after an instrumental in the sense of] 'he gambles with it', 'he digs with it', 'he wins with it', or 'won by it':
After vasna-kraya-vikraya, the affix ṭhan [occurs in the sense of 'lives by'].
After vivadha and vīvadha, [the affix ṣṭhan occurs] optionally (vibhāṣā) [in the sense of 'carries'].
After apamitya and yācita, the affixes kak and kan [occur respectively in the sense of 'brought about by'].
[The affix ṭhak occurs] in the sense of 'proceeds with vigor, strength, or water'.
[The affix ṭhak occurs in the sense of 'proceeds along'] that which is prefixed with prati or anu and followed by īpa, loma, or kūla.
[The affix ṭhak occurs after a nominal stem in the accusative case in the sense of] 'kills birds, fish, or beasts'.
And [the affix ṭhak occurs in the sense of] 'stands [as] an obstacle'.
[The affix ṭhak occurs in the sense of] 'runs' after a stem ending in mātha, or after padavī or anupada.
[The affix ṭhak occurs] in the sense of 'goes along the contrary path', and the affix ṭhañ also.
After maḍḍuka and jharjhara, the affix aṇ occurs optionally (anyatarasyām) [in the sense of 'that is his craft'].
[The affix ṭhak occurs in the sense of] 'whose belief is: "it exists", "it does not exist", or "it is fated"'.
After a stem having a poly-syllabic prior member, the affix ṭhac [occurs in the sense of 'conduct in religious act or study'].
[The affix ṭhac occurs in the sense of] 'that is regularly given to him'.
[The affix ṭhac occurs in the sense of] 'he deals in' [kaṭhina], or 'he acts in' kaṭhina, an extension, or a settlement.
[The affix yat occurs in the sense of] 'he bears that', [after stems denoting] a chariot, a yoke, or a side-yoke.
[The affix] ñya occurs [after a stem] combined with gṛhapati [in the sense of 'joined with'].

After nau, vayas, dharma, viṣa, mūla, mūla, sītā, and tulā, [the affix yat occurs respectively] in the meanings 'to be crossed', 'equal', 'attainable', 'to be killed', 'to be bent', 'equal', 'furrowed', and 'weighed'.
After dharma, pathin, artha, and nyāya, [the affix yat occurs in the sense of] 'not departing from that'.
After mata, jana, and hala, [the affix yat occurs respectively] in the meanings 'instrument', 'prattle', and 'furrowing'.
After pathin, atithi, vasati, and svapati, [the affix] ḍhañ [occurs in the sense of 'skilled therein'].
After veśanta and himavat, [the affix] aṇ [occurs in the sense of 'existing there' in the Veda].
After srotas, [the affixes] ḍyat and ḍya occur optionally (vibhāṣā) [in the sense of 'existing there' in the Veda].
After sagarbha, sayūtha, and sanuta, [the affix] yan [occurs in the sense of 'existing there' in the Veda].
After revatī, jagatī, and haviṣyā, [the affix yat occurs in the Veda] in the sense of 'praiseworthy'.

4.4.s: tadvān āsām upadhāno mantra iti iṣṭakāsu luk ca matoḥ ||
4.4.d: तद्वान् आसाम् उपधानो मन्त्र इति इष्टकासु लुक् च मतोः ॥

4.4.m: [The affix] matup [occurs] after [the stem] mūrdhan- [in the sense 'the mantra containing that is the laying-formula for these'], when referring to vayasyā [bricks].
[The affix] yal [occurs] after [the stems] veśas-, yaśas-, and the rest, and after bhaga- [in the same sense].
And [the affixes] ina and ya [occur after a stem in the third case in the sense] 'made by ancestors'.
[The affix] gha occurs [after a stem in the third case in the sense] 'measured by a thousand'.
[The affix tātil occurs after the stems] śiva-, śam-, and ariṣṭa- in the sense of an agent who causes [them].

5.1.m: And [the affix yat occurs in that sense] after [the stems] khala-, yava-, māṣa-, tila-, vṛṣa-, and brahman-.
[The affixes] ṇa and ḍhañ [occur in that sense] respectively after [the stems] sarva- and puruṣa-.
[The affix] khañ occurs [in that sense] after [the stems] māṇava- and caraka-.
[The affixes occur] after [a stem denoting] the raw material [in the fourth case in the sense] 'for the purpose of that modification'.
[The affix] ḍhañ [occurs in that sense] after [the stems] chadis-, upadhi-, and bali-.

5.1.s: tad asya tad asmin syād iti ||
5.1.d: तद् अस्य तद् अस्मिन् स्याद् इति ॥
5.1.m: [The affixes occur after a stem in the first case in the sense] 'that would be of this/him' or 'that would be in this/him'.
And [the affixes] ṭhan and yat [occur] after [the stem] śata- when it does not refer to a hundred [coins/measures].
[The affix] añ occurs optionally (anyatarasyām) after [the stem] śūrpa-.
[The affix] aṇ occurs after [the stems] śatamāna-, viṃśatika-, sahasra-, and vasana-.
[The zero-replacement (luk) applies] optionally (vibhāṣā) after [the stems] kārṣāpaṇa- and sahasra- [in a dvigu compound].
[The affix] yat occurs after [the stems] paṇa-, pāda-, māṣa-, and śata- [preceded by dvi- or tri-].
[The affixes] aṇ and añ [occur respectively] after sarvabhūmi and pṛthivī.

5.1.s: tad dharati vahavty āvahati bhārād vaṃśādibhyaḥ ||
5.1.d: तद् धरति वहव्त्य् आवहति भाराद् वंशादिभ्यः ॥

5.1.m: [The affixes] ṭhan and kan [occur respectively] after vasna and dravya.
[The affix occurs in the senses of] 'holds [that]', 'takes off [that]', or 'cooks [that]'.
[The forms] paṅkti, viṃśati, triṃśat, catvāriṃśat, pañcāśat, ṣaṣṭi, saptati, aśīti, navati, and śata [are irregularly formed to denote measure].
[The forms] pañcat and daśat [are irregularly formed] optionally when designating a collective group.
[The affix] ḍaṇ [occurs] after triṃśat and catvāriṃśat in a Brāhmaṇa text when denoting a name.
And [the affix] cha occurs after kaḍaṅkara ('straw') and dakṣiṇā ('sacrificial fee').
[The affixes] gha and khañ occur respectively after yajña ('sacrifice') and ṛtvij ('priest').
And [the affix ṇa occurs after uttarapatha] in the sense 'brought by the northern route (uttarapatha)'.
[The affix occurs in the sense of one who is] appointed, hired, existing, or about to exist for that [time, denoted by an accusative word].
[The affixes] yat and khañ occur after māsa ('month') when age (vayas) is denoted.
[The word] ṣaṣṭika- [is irregularly derived] in the sense of '[rice] that matures in sixty nights'.
In the Veda, [the affix] cha occurs after [a stem] ending in vatsara ('year').
[The affix occurs after a stem denoting time in the instrumental in the senses:] to be conquered, obtainable, to be done, or easy to do by it.
And [the affix occurs in the sense] 'the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) of that [time]' after words denoting a sacrifice.
And [the affix occurs] in the sense 'given therein' or 'to be done therein', as in the rules concerning bhavat ('being present therein').
[The affixes] ṇa and yat occur respectively after yathākathāca and hasta with the instrumental sense [of 'given therein' or 'to be done therein'].
[The affix occurs in the sense] 'the proper time for that has arrived' after a nominal stem in the genitive case.
[The affix cha occurs in the sense of 'purpose'] after samāpana ('completion') when it has an initial member (sapūrvapada).
[The form] ākālika- [is irregularly formed with the affix ṭhañ] when stating [the simultaneous occurrence of] the beginning and the end.
[The secondary affix] vati occurs after [a stem ending in the instrumental] in the sense 'equal to that', if it is an action.
In the Veda, [the affix vati occurs] after a prefix (upasarga) in the sense of a verbal root.
[The affixes taught up to 5.1.119 do] not [apply] after a tatpuruṣa compound preceded by the negative particle nañ, except after acatura, asaṅgata, alavaṇa, avaṭa, abudha, akata, arasa, and alasa.
[The affix] imanij optionally occurs after pṛthu and the like [in the sense of 'the state of being that'].
And [the affix ṣyañ occurs] after words denoting qualities (guṇavacana) and after brāhmaṇa and the like in the sense of action (karman) [as well as 'state of being that'].
After that which ends in pati, and after the class headed by purohita, the affix yak [is introduced].
After that which ends in hāyana, and after the class headed by yuvan, the affix aṇ [is introduced].

5.2.m: In the sense of a field where it grows, after terms denoting grains, the affix khañ [is introduced].
After yava, yavaka, and ṣaṣṭika, the affix yat [is introduced].
After sarvacarman, the affixes kha and khañ [are introduced in the sense of] 'made [thereof]'.
[The affix kha is introduced in the sense of] 'pervading that' after pathin, aṅga, karman, patra, and pātra, preceded by sarva.
[The affix kha is introduced after parovara, parampara, and putrapautra] in the sense of 'experiencing'.
After goṣṭha, the affix khañ [is introduced] in the sense of 'formerly situated in'.
In the sense of its ripening or its root, the affixes kuṇap and jāhac [are introduced] after the classes headed by pīlu and karṇa respectively.
In the sense of 'famous for that', the affixes cuñcup and caṇap [are introduced].
After vi and nañ, the affixes nā and nāñ [are introduced], with the substitute nasa [for nāsikā].
In the sense of measure, the affixes dvayasac, daghnañ, and mātrac [are introduced].
And after puruṣa and hastin, the affix aṇ [is introduced in the sense of measure].
After yad, tad, and eta, the affix vatup [is introduced] in the sense of quantity.

5.2.s: tad asminn adhikam iti daśāntāḍ ḍaḥ ||
5.2.d: तद् अस्मिन्न् अधिकम् इति दशान्ताड् डः ॥
5.2.m: In the sense of 'that is added to this', the affix ḍa [is introduced] after that which ends in daśan.
[The augment] thuk [is added] after ṣaṣ, kati, katipaya, and catur.
After viṃśati and the like, [the affix] tamaṭ occurs optionally (anyatarasyām).
When [a hymn is in] an appraisal [meter], [the affix] cha occurs [to designate] a sūkta or a sāman.
[When denoting] 'comprehension so many times', there is optionally zero-replacement (luk) [of the affix ḍaṭ etc.].
After śṛṅkhala [in the sense of] 'its fetter', [ṭhak occurs] when referring to a young camel.
Śrotriya [is irregularly formed in the sense of] 'one who studies the sacred metre'.
In sacred text, paripanthin and pariparin [are irregularly formed in the sense of] 'an adversary'.
Kṣetriya [is formed with the affix] ghac in [the sense of] 'incurable / to be treated in another's field'.
Indriya [is formed] optionally (vā) in [the sense of] 'an indication of Indra', 'seen by Indra', 'created by Indra', 'enjoyed by Indra', or 'given by Indra'.

5.2.s: tad asya asty asminn iti matup ||
5.2.d: तद् अस्य अस्त्य् अस्मिन्न् इति मतुप् ॥

5.2.m: After [a stem ending in] long ā denoting a bodily limb, [the affix] lac occurs optionally (anyatarasyām).
After vatsa and aṃsa, [lac occurs] in [the sense of] 'affection' and 'strength' [respectively].
And [the affix aṇ occurs] after sikatā and śarkarā.
After ūṣa, suṣi, muṣka, and madhu, [the affix] ra [occurs].
[The affix] valac [occurs] after rajas, kṛṣi, āsuti, and pariṣad.
[The words] jyotsnā, tamisrā, śṛṅgiṇa, ūrjasvin, ūrjasvala, gomin, malina, and malīmasa [are irregularly formed in the sense of 'possessing that'].
[The affix] ṭhañ [occurs] obligatorily after [a stem] preceded by eka or go.
[The affix] yap [occurs] after rūpa in the senses of 'struck' or 'praised'.
[The affix] vini [occurs] after [stems ending in] -as, and after māyā, medhā, and sraj.
[The affixes] ālac and āṭac [occur after vāc] in the sense of 'one who speaks excessively'.
And also after [stems] ending in dharma, śīla, or varṇa.
[The affix] matup optionally [occurs] after stems belonging to the class headed by bala.

5.3.m: [These affixes occur] after kim, pronouns, and bahu, excluding those from dvi onwards.
sa optionally replaces sarva before [an affix beginning with] d.
[The affix] rhil occurs optionally [after idam and tad in the sense of time] not referring to the current day.
sadyaḥ, parut, parāri, aiṣamaḥ, paredyavi, adya, pūrvedyuḥ, anyedyuḥ, anyataredyuḥ, itaredyuḥ, aparedyuḥ, adharedyuḥ, ubhayedyuḥ, and uttaredyuḥ [are irregular formations denoting time].
[The affix] astāti occurs after directional words ending in the seventh, fifth, or first inflectional ending in [the sense of] direction, place, or time.
[The affix aṇ occurs] before eleven in non-Vedic texts [after ordinals in tīya denoting part].
And [the affix] kan and zero-replacement (luk) [occur after ordinals in the sense of part] when referring to a measure or a limb of an animal.
[The affixes] tamap and iṣṭhan [occur] in [the sense of] excellence or superlative degree.
neda and sādha are [the substitutes] of antika and bāḍha [respectively, before the affixes beginning with a vowel].
[The affixes] kalpab, deśya, and deśīyar [occur] in [the sense of] slight incompleteness.
[The affix] jātīyar [occurs] in the expression of kind or manner.
Of indeclinables (avyaya) and pronouns (sarvanāman), akac [occurs] prior to the final vowel sequence (ṭi).
And according to the Easterners, after [a name] beginning with a preposition (upa-ādi), [the affixes] aḍac and vuc [occur].
After kuṭī, śamī, and śuṇḍā, [the affix] ra [occurs in the sense of smallness].
After kim, yad, and tad, when singling out one from two, [the affix] ḍatarac [is introduced].
After ekaśālā, [the affix] ṭhañ [is] optionally (anyatarasyām) [introduced in the sense of 'like'].
After [a stem denoting a] pūga, [the affix] ñya [is introduced], provided it is not preceded by grāmaṇī.
After stems with the affix cphañ denoting a vrāta, [the affix ñya is introduced], except when feminine.
After [a stem denoting] a martial clan (āyudhajīvisaṅgha) among the Vāhīkas, except a Brāhmaṇa or Rājanya, [the affix] ñyaṇ [is introduced].
After parśvādi and yaudheyādi, [the affixes] aṇ and añ [are introduced] respectively.
After abhijit, vidabhṛt, śālāvat, śikhāvat, śamīvat, ūrṇāvat, śarumat, and stems with the affix aṇ, [the affix] yañ [is introduced].

5.4.s: pādaśatasya saṅkhyāder vīpsāyāṃ vun lopaś ca ||
5.4.d: पादशतस्य सङ्ख्यादेर् वीप्सायां वुन् लोपश् च ॥

5.4.m: And when punishment (daṇḍa) or abandonment (vyavasarga) is expressed [vun and elision are introduced after pādaśata preceded by a numeral].
After sthūla, etc., denoting kind or degree (prakāravacana), [the affix] kan [is introduced].
After [a word] ending in jāti, [the affix] cha [is introduced] in the sense of a kinsman (bandhu).
After bahu, [the affix] dhā is optionally (vibhāṣā) [introduced] when time is not remote.
In the sense of 'that is present in abundance' (prakṛtavacane), [the affix] mayaṭ [is introduced].
After [a word] ending in devatā, for the purpose thereof (tādarthya), [the affix] yat [is introduced].
In relation to a counter-entity (pratiyoga), [the affix] tasi [substitutes] for the ablative (pañcamī).
In [the senses of] excessive grasp, non-pain, and reproach, [tasi substitutes] for an instrumental (tṛtīyā) not expressing the agent (akartṛ).

When a thing becomes what it previously was not (abhūtatadbhāva), in construction with kṛ ('to make'), bhū ('to become'), and as ('to be'), [the affix] cvi [occurs] after [a nominal stem denoting] the agent that attains [that state] (sampadyakartṛ).
And there is elision (lopa) of [the final s of] arus, manas, cakṣus, cetas, rahas, and rajas [before cvi].
[The affix trā occurs] variously (bahulam) after deva, manuṣya, puruṣa, puru, and martya, [substituting] for the accusative (dvitīyā) and locative (saptamī) endings.
After an imitative sound (avyaktānukaraṇa) consisting of at least two vowels, not ending in iti, [the affix] ḍāc [occurs before kṛ, bhū, and as].
In [the sense of] ploughing (kṛṣi), [the affix ḍāc occurs] after dvitīya, tṛtīya, śamba, and bīja, in construction with kṛñ ('to do/make').
[The compound-final affix a occurs] after ṛc, pur, ap, dhur, and pathin, [in a tatpuruṣa compound], when not expressing an axle.
[The compound-final affix] ac [occurs] after sāman and loman preceded by prati, anu, or ava.

[The forms] acatura, vicatura, sucatura, strīpuṃsa, dhenvanaḍuha, ṛkṣāma, vāṅmanasa, akṣibhruva, dāragava, ūrvaṣṭhīva, padaṣṭhīva, naktaṃdiva, rātriṃdiva, ahardiva, sarajasa, niḥśreyasa, puruṣāyuṣa, dvyāyuṣa, tryāyuṣa, ṛgyajuṣa, jātokṣa, mahokṣa, vṛddhokṣa, upaśuna, and goṣṭhaśva [are irregularly formed with the affix ac].
[The affix ac occurs] after varcas preceded by brahma or hastin.
[The affix ac occurs] after tamas preceded by ava, sam, or andha.
[The affix ac occurs] after vasīyas and śreyas preceded by śvas.
[The affix ac occurs] after uras standing in the locative case, preceded by prati.
And [the affix ṭac occurs] after takṣan preceded by grāma or kuṭī.
And [the affix ṭac occurs] after sakthi preceded by uttara or mṛga.
In the sacred texts (chandas), [the affix ṭac occurs] after a neuter [stem] ending in an or as.
[The affix ṭac occurs] after brahman when naming a region.
[The affix ṭac occurs after brahman] optionally (anyatarasyām) preceded by ku or mahat.
[The affix ṭac occurs] in an avyayībhāva compound after śarad and the like.
[The affix ṭac occurs] optionally (anyatarasyām) after a neuter [stem ending in an in an avyayībhāva compound].
[The affix ṭac occurs in an avyayībhāva compound] optionally after a river name, paurṇamāsī, and āgrahāyaṇī.
In a bahuvrīhi compound, [the affix] ṣac [occurs] after sakthi and akṣi when denoting a part of one's own body.
[The affix] ṣa [occurs] after mūrdhan preceded by dvi or tri.
And [the affix ap occurs] after loman preceded by antar or bahis.

5.4.s: añ nāsikāyāḥ sañjñāyāṃ nasaṃ ca asthūlāt ||
5.4.d: अञ् नासिकायाः सञ्ज्ञायां नसं च अस्थूलात् ॥

5.4.m: [The forms] suprāta, suśva, sudiva, śārikukṣa, caturaśra, eṇīpada, ājapada, and proṣṭhapada [are irregularly formed with the affix ac].
[The affix] asic obligatorily [occurs] after prajā and medhā [preceded by nañ, dur, or su].
[The affix anic occurs after jambhā, with substitution of] jambha, preceded by su, harita, tṛṇa, or soma.
[The affix anic does] not [occur] after dakṣiṇā when connected with lubdha ('hunter').
There is elision (lopa) of [the final part of] pāda ('foot'), except after hastin and others.
And [datṛ is optionally the substitute for danta] after agra, anta, śuddha, śubhra, vṛṣa, and varāha.
[The compound-ending affix] kap [occurs] after [words of the class] headed by uras ('chest').
